1. Infrastructure as Code, Defined
Infrastructure as Code, IaC, means managing real, genuine infrastructure through code files, rather than through manual, real, live console interactions.
This real, broader concept existed before Terraform, and includes several genuinely different, real tools, Terraform among the most widely, actually adopted.
This connects directly back to What is Terraform, already covered, Terraform is genuinely one, concrete, real, practical implementation of this idea.

blocks.content: 4. Real Repeatability
The same, real code file, run genuinely across many, different, real environments, dev, staging, production, produces genuinely consistent, matching infrastructure.

IaC splits into two, real, genuinely different approaches, declarative, describing the desired end state, and imperative, describing the exact, real steps.

7. The Real Code Becomes the Source of Truth
blocks.text: 7. The Real Code Becomes the Source of Truth

blocks.content: Once real infrastructure is managed through IaC, the genuine code itself becomes the honest, real source of truth, not memory, and not the live console.
This real shift changes how a genuine team should verify infrastructure, checking the real code, rather than manually inspecting the real, live environment.
This connects directly to State, covered in complete, real depth in a dedicated module later in this course, Terraform's own, real record of reality.
This real, honest source of truth is worth protecting carefully, manual, undocumented changes genuinely undermine this entire, foundational idea.

blocks.content: 8. Real Infrastructure Drift, Introduced Briefly
Real infrastructure drift happens when the genuine, live environment no longer matches what the code describes, introduced here only briefly, for now.
This real, important concept is covered in genuine, complete depth in the State module, and again in the Drift Detection topic, later in this course.
Understanding that drift is genuinely possible, even with IaC in place, sets real, honest, practical expectations, rather than assuming code alone prevents it.
This real, honest acknowledgment is worth making early, IaC is a genuinely powerful discipline, not an automatic, perfect, real guarantee.

blocks.content: 10. A Real, Common Mistake
Mixing manual, live console changes with real, IaC-managed resources is a real, common, and genuinely risky mistake, undermining the source-of-truth idea.
This often happens under real, urgent pressure, a quick, manual fix feels faster, but genuinely creates drift, already covered, that code no longer reflects.
The honest fix is committing fully, real, once a resource is managed by IaC, every, genuine change should flow through that, same, real code path.
This mistake is worth guarding against directly, exactly the same, honest discipline already emphasized throughout the Why Terraform topic, earlier in this module.
